answers.brief_reasoning: Use two private int instance variables. use() clamps the amount to the current level and returns the amount actually used.
Keep adding n % 10 to a running sum and dividing n by 10 until n reaches 0. When n is 0 the loop never runs, so the method returns 0.

Start at start and count upward until n % digitSum(n) == 0. Because start >= 1, the digit sum is never 0, so there is no divide-by-zero. The loop always stops, because every number from 1 to 9 is divisible by its own digit sum, and so is every power of 10.
